title: Potential Increase in Spatial Overlap Between Humans and Large Carnivore Species Under Future Climate Change Scenarios in the Sanjiangyuan Region, China未来气候变化可能导致中国三江源地区人类与大型食肉动物的空间重叠进一步增加
content:
By evaluating the impacts of climate change on habitat suitability and delineating potential human–wildlife spatial overlap areas for four large carnivores in the Sanjiangyuan Region, this study projects that future climate change will exacerbate habitat fragmentation, necessitating the re-evaluation and optimization of the protected area network. Furthermore, the findings indicate a heightened risk of conflict between local communities and brown bears, a critical issue that warrants special attention.


ABSTRACT

Climate change-driven resource scarcity is likely to intensify human–wildlife conflicts (HWC) through increased spatial overlap between humans and wildlife. Therefore, assessing wildlife habitat suitability under climate change and evaluating species vulnerability are essential for improving in-situ conservation planning. This study predicts climate change impacts on habitat suitability for four large carnivores, including the snow leopard Panthera uncia, wolf Canis lupus, brown bear Ursus arctos, and Eurasian lynx Lynx lynx, in the Sanjiangyuan Region of China, assessing their vulnerability and protection gaps. Our findings showed: (1) under current conditions, the Sanjiangyuan region offered the largest suitable habitat for wolves, followed by snow leopards and Eurasian lynx, with brown bears having the smallest area; (2) by 2030S (SSP126), snow leopards and wolves faced the most severe impacts, with ~7.73% and ~6.40% of their habitat becoming vulnerable; (3) future climate change was expected to significantly affect brown bears, potentially increasing high, medium, and low suitability habitats by ~4.5, ~5.6, and ~2.8 times by 2070S; (4) Eurasian lynx habitat was projected to increase slightly, most notably by 2070S under SSP126 (RScf = 22.50%); (5) Spatial overlap between human and large carnivore activities is projected to be concentrated primarily in the central and southern Sanjiangyuan region under future climate scenarios, with climate change potentially expanding risks for human-brown bear and human-Eurasian lynx conflicts; (6) Protection gaps for all four species were concentrated in northeastern Tanggulashan Town, southern Qumalai County, and southeastern Zhiduo County. These findings offer crucial data for large carnivore conservation, national park planning, and the formulation of evidence-based strategies to mitigate HWC.

气候变化引发的资源短缺可能会导致人类活动空间与野生动物分布范围的空间重叠持续扩大, 进而可能加剧人兽冲突问题。因此, 科学评估气候变化情景下野生动物栖息地适宜性动态变化并系统识别物种脆弱性评估, 是优化就地保护规划的关键前提。本研究系统评估了气候变化对中国三江源地区四种大型食肉动物 (雪豹、狼、棕熊和猞猁) 栖息地适宜性的潜在影响, 并进一步开展物种脆弱性评估和当前的保护空缺分析。研究结果表明: (1) 当前气候条件下, 狼的适宜栖息地面积最大, 其次为雪豹和猞猁, 棕熊最小； (2) 至2030S年代 (SSP126情境下), 雪豹和狼的适宜栖息地收缩最为显著, 预计分别丧失约7.73%与6.40%； (3) 棕熊对气候变化响应最为敏感, 至2070S年代, 其高、中、低适宜栖息地面积较当前分别增加约4.5倍、5.6倍和2.8倍； (4) 猞猁适宜栖息地呈温和扩张趋势, 2070S年代增幅最为明显 (RS cf = 22.50%) ； (5) 未来人类活动空间与四种大型食肉动物分布区的重叠区域主要集中在三江源的中部和南部, 而人类与棕熊和猞猁之间的冲突风险将进一步加剧； (6) 四种大型食肉动物的保护空缺区域主要集中于唐古拉山镇东北部、曲麻莱县南部及治多县东南部。本研究结果可为大型食肉动物适应性保护策略制定、国家公园规划以及人兽冲突缓解措施的制定提供关键的数据支持 。
